block.airwaves.speaker: Speaker
tooltip.airwaves.board.computer_board: Any circuit with a microchip: remembers and counts
tooltip.airwaves.board.sensor_board: Any circuit with a sensor: reacts to the world
gui.airwaves.part.resistor: Next to a capacitor: timer. Transistor: amplifier. Tube: tube amp. LED: indicator
gui.airwaves.part.capacitor: Next to a coil: tuned tank. Crystal: oscillator. Resistor: timer
gui.airwaves.part.led: Next to a resistor: indicator (lights the box lamp)
gui.airwaves.part.transistor: Next to a resistor: amplifier. Another transistor: logic gate
gui.airwaves.part.tube: Next to a resistor: tube amplifier
gui.airwaves.part.coil: Next to a capacitor: tuned tank (listens to a station)
gui.airwaves.part.crystal: Next to a capacitor: oscillator (a clock, or blink)
gui.airwaves.part.memory_chip: A stage on its own: every new signal flips it on or off
gui.airwaves.part.counter_chip: A stage on its own: counts signals, outputs the count
gui.airwaves.part.pulse_chip: A stage on its own: turns a signal into one short tick
gui.airwaves.part.light_sensor: A stage on its own: daylight. First: the source. Later: only by day
gui.airwaves.part.rain_sensor: A stage on its own: rain. First: the source. Later: only in rain
gui.airwaves.part.motion_sensor: A stage on its own: a player within 8 blocks
gui.airwaves.part.copper: Copper trace: joins parts into stages
tooltip.airwaves.board.logic_board: Any working circuit: runs in a Circuit Box
gui.airwaves.workbench.pick: Click: make this kind of board
gui.airwaves.workbench.blueprint_hint: One circuit that works for it. Many others do too.
tooltip.airwaves.portable_radio.use: Right-click: on / off. Sneak + right-click: next station. Talk while holding it: walkie-talkie
gui.airwaves.workbench.open: Join IN to OUT with copper
gui.airwaves.workbench.loose: Some parts are not on the circuit
gui.airwaves.workbench.unknown: These parts don't make a known board
gui.airwaves.workbench.need_blank: It works! Add a blank board
gui.airwaves.workbench.howto: Parts that touch, or are joined by copper, make stages. The stages decide what the board can be.
gui.airwaves.workbench.draw_hint:
Click or drag: draw a copper trace
Right-click: erase
gui.airwaves.workbench.erase_hint: Click or right-click: erase this trace
gui.airwaves.workbench.in: Input pads: the circuit starts here
gui.airwaves.workbench.out: Output pads: the circuit must reach one of these
airwaves.ponder.tag.radio.description: Transmitters, receivers and everything that carries a voice over the air
airwaves.ponder.transmitter_setup.text_1: Transmitters need a block of Copper placed directly behind them. Any Copper block works, even weathered or waxed
airwaves.ponder.transmitter_setup.text_2: An Antenna of the same size as the Transmitter has to stand on that Copper. It needs to be at least 4 layers tall
airwaves.ponder.transmitter_setup.text_3: The taller the Antenna, the further it reaches. A small Antenna 4 tall reaches about 600 blocks, 10 tall about 1700, and 20 tall about 3700
airwaves.ponder.transmitter_setup.text_4: Right-click the glass dome with Amethyst to fill the Crystal Chamber. An Amethyst Block gives a 10 percent cleaner signal than a shard
airwaves.ponder.transmitter_setup.text_5: Transmitters are powered by Rotational Force. Connect a shaft to the left or right side. They need at least 16 RPM
airwaves.ponder.transmitter_setup.text_6: 64 RPM gives full range, and 128 RPM gives 1.5 times the range. Stress per RPM: Small 4, Medium 8, Large 16, Giant 32
airwaves.ponder.transmitter_setup.text_7: Once running, it broadcasts anyone talking within 2.5 blocks of it, or anything said into a cabled Microphone
airwaves.ponder.transmitter_setup.text_8: A Redstone signal puts it on standby. Engineer's Goggles show its range and anything it is missing
airwaves.ponder.transmitter_microphone.t: Microphones let you broadcast from further away, like from a studio or a stage
Use a Wire on the Microphone, then on the jack of the Transmitter, to connect them
Wires only carry sound. Copper reaches 16 blocks, Gold 24, Silver 32 and Fiber 64. Better Wires lose less quality
Anyone within 3.5 blocks of the Microphone is now on air. A glowing pulse runs along the Wire while they talk
Sneak-click a connector to take its cables down. You get the Wires back
airwaves.ponder.receiver_setup.header: Receivers, Speakers and the PA Horn
airwaves.ponder.receiver_setup.text_1: Receivers pick up one station and play it out loud
airwaves.ponder.receiver_setup.text_2: They need an Antenna of the same size, placed on top of them or on a Copper block behind them. Copper behind adds 25 percent more gain
airwaves.ponder.receiver_setup.text_3: Fill the Crystal Chamber with Amethyst to switch it on. An Amethyst Block gives 15 percent more gain. Receivers do not need any Rotational Force
airwaves.ponder.receiver_setup.text_4: Use an item tuned at the Tuning Table to set which station it plays
airwaves.ponder.receiver_setup.text_5: Speakers cabled to a Receiver play its sound. One Receiver can drive many Speakers
airwaves.ponder.receiver_setup.text_6: PA Horns work just like Speakers, and are made for walls and poles outside
airwaves.ponder.receiver_setup.text_7: Receivers also give out a Redstone signal from 0 to 15. The stronger the station, the stronger the signal
airwaves.ponder.antennas_stacking.text_1: Antennas are built upwards. Keep placing the same Antenna on top to make it taller
airwaves.ponder.antennas_stacking.text_2: The top layer always gets a cap with a beacon light
airwaves.ponder.antennas_stacking.text_3: Bigger Antennas are wider: Medium is 2x2, Big is 4x4 and Giant is 8x8. One item places a whole layer at once
airwaves.ponder.antennas_stacking.text_4: Small Antennas grow up to 20 layers and Medium up to 40. Big ones reach 64 and Giant ones 96, getting narrower near the top
airwaves.ponder.antennas_stacking.text_5: Taller masts give more range and a cleaner signal. They can also be climbed like ladders
airwaves.ponder.cables_insulators.text_1: Every type of Wire has a maximum length. If two blocks are too far apart, the cable cannot be placed
airwaves.ponder.cables_insulators.text_2: Glass Insulators hold cables in between, so a line can go much further. Each one holds up to 4 cables, so a line can also split here
airwaves.ponder.cables_insulators.text_3: Each block of Wire adds a little noise. Copper is the noisiest, and Fiber has no noise at all
airwaves.ponder.cables_insulators.text_4: Any Airwaves cable joins any other at an insulator. With Power Grid installed they carry its electricity too
airwaves.ponder.radio_tower_drive.text_1: The Radio Tower is a complete broadcasting station, with a 27 block tall Antenna built in. It reaches about 38000 blocks. This is its base
airwaves.ponder.radio_tower_drive.text_2: A drive shaft runs from the cabinet in the middle out to both edges of the base
airwaves.ponder.radio_tower_drive.text_3: Connect Rotational Force to either end of the drive shaft. The Radio Tower needs 64 stress per RPM
airwaves.ponder.radio_tower_drive.text_4: Right-click near the cabinet with Amethyst to fill its Crystal Chamber. Once it has power and Amethyst, it goes on air
airwaves.ponder.radio_tower_drive.text_5: Cable a Microphone to the cabinet to broadcast. A Redstone signal on the cabinet puts it on standby
airwaves.ponder.relay_tower_drive.text_1: Relay Towers pick up a station and send it out again from where they stand. The Relay Tower reaches about 5600 blocks, the Big Relay Tower about 14500
airwaves.ponder.relay_tower_drive.text_2: Like the Radio Tower, they are powered through the drive shaft in their base. The Relay Tower needs 12 stress per RPM, the Big Relay Tower 24
airwaves.ponder.relay_tower_drive.text_3: Use a tuned item on the Relay Tower to set which station it passes on
airwaves.ponder.relay_tower_drive.text_4: Relays can be chained up to 4 times. They only pass on stations heard with at least 20 percent quality. A Redstone signal switches them off
airwaves.ponder.jammer_basics.text_1: This Radio is playing a station clearly
airwaves.ponder.jammer_basics.text_2: Signal Jammers are powered by Rotational Force, just like Transmitters. They need 8 stress per RPM
airwaves.ponder.jammer_basics.text_3: When given a Redstone signal, every station within 48 blocks turns into static. The closer, the worse
airwaves.ponder.jammer_basics.text_4: It also works as a barrier: any signal passing within 48 blocks on its way to a radio is jammed too. Only the Creative Receiver ignores Jammers
airwaves.ponder.yagi_antenna.header: Yagi Antennas: Radio with a Direction
airwaves.ponder.yagi_antenna.text_1: An ordinary antenna mast sends its station out the same way all round
airwaves.ponder.yagi_antenna.text_2: Clamp a Yagi Antenna on top of the mast and it becomes a beam. The Yagi points the way you face when you place it
airwaves.ponder.yagi_antenna.text_3: Straight ahead the station reaches 1.9 times as far as before
airwaves.ponder.yagi_antenna.text_4: To the sides it reaches about a third, and right behind barely an eighth: a real blind spot
airwaves.ponder.yagi_antenna.text_5: On a receiver's mast it listens the same way. Point two Yagis at each other for a long link that stations around you do not hear
airwaves.ponder.workbench_boards.text_1: Every circuit board is soldered at the Circuit Workbench. There are no recipes: you design each circuit yourself
airwaves.ponder.workbench_boards.text_2: Slot a Blank Circuit Board into the bench, then lay parts out on its 8 by 5 grid
airwaves.ponder.workbench_boards.text_3: Parts that touch work together. A coil beside a capacitor is a tuned tank, a crystal beside a capacitor an oscillator
airwaves.ponder.workbench_boards.text_4: Then draw copper from the IN pads on the left to the OUT pads on the right. The moment it carries, the bench lists its stages
airwaves.ponder.workbench_boards.text_5: The stages decide every kind of board this circuit can become. Pick one of them, then take the finished board out
airwaves.ponder.workbench_boards.text_6: Add a transistor amplifier and an LED indicator, and the same tuner can now be a Radio Board too
airwaves.ponder.workbench_boards.text_7: Stages can sit anywhere, as long as the copper joins them. Their order from IN to OUT matters later
airwaves.ponder.workbench_boards.text_8: Three indicators make a Display Board. Any circuit that carries can at least be a Logic Board
airwaves.ponder.workbench_boards.text_9: Every board keeps the circuit you soldered, and shows it on its icon. Two boards of the same kind can still behave differently
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.header: Boards that Run on their Own
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.text_1: A Circuit Box runs any board on its own. Redstone goes in at its back, and the result comes out of its front
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.text_2: The board inside is its program, read from IN to OUT. This one: redstone in, two timers, out
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.text_3: Flick the lever back, and the timers hold the light on for two more seconds
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.text_4: Two transistors side by side are a logic gate, which inverts: the lamp is on until the lever is pulled
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.text_5: With a crystal oscillator first, the board is a clock: the box pulses on its own. Every extra crystal slows it down
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.text_6: With a tuned tank first, the board listens. Tune the box like a receiver, and it gives a signal while that station is on the air
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.text_7: Indicators on the board light the lamp on the box itself, so you can see it working
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.text_8: Microchips and sensors need no partner. A motion sensor, a pulse chip and a counter chip: it counts everyone who walks past
airwaves.ponder.circuit_box.text_9: The output strength is the count so far, ready for a comparator or a lamp chain
airwaves.ponder.dimensional_relay.text_1: Radio waves never cross into another dimension on their own. A station in the Overworld cannot be heard in the Nether or the End
airwaves.ponder.dimensional_relay.text_2: A Dimensional Relay carries them across. Build it where it can hear the stations you want to send
airwaves.ponder.dimensional_relay.text_3: Like every Airwaves machine it runs on Rotational Force, 16 stress per RPM, or on electricity through its built-in red + and blue - terminals
airwaves.ponder.dimensional_relay.text_4: On its own it has no partner yet
airwaves.ponder.dimensional_relay.text_5: Build a second Dimensional Relay in the Nether or the End, and power it the same way. The two link up on their own
airwaves.ponder.dimensional_relay.text_6: Now every station one relay hears is sent out again by the other, on its own frequency. It works both ways
airwaves.ponder.dimensional_relay.text_7: A Radio in the Nether can now tune in to Overworld stations, and stations in the Nether reach the Overworld
airwaves.ponder.dimensional_relay.text_8: A running relay keeps its own chunk loaded, so the link never drops. A Redstone signal switches it off
airwaves.ponder.dimensional_relay.text_9: Engineer's Goggles show which dimensions a relay is linked to, and how many stations it sends and brings in
airwaves.ponder.radio_basics.text_1: Right-click a Radio to switch it on or off
airwaves.ponder.radio_basics.text_2: Sneak-click it to jump to the next station it can hear
airwaves.ponder.radio_basics.text_3: Radios stay quiet until someone talks. Distance and bad weather add static
airwaves.ponder.radio_basics.text_4: The Tuning Table sets the frequency of radio items. AM goes from 530 to 1700 kHz, FM from 87.5 to 108 MHz
airwaves.ponder.radio_basics.text_5: It also shows which stations can be heard, and how far your own station reaches
airwaves.ponder.radio_basics.text_6: Only blocks on exactly the same frequency can hear each other. Rename an item in an Anvil to name your station
airwaves.ponder.radio_basics.text_7: The Portable Radio plays the station straight into your ears while it is in your hotbar. Sneak-click it to jump to the next station
airwaves.ponder.airship_console.text_1: All radio blocks work on Aeronautics airships, and use where the ship really is
airwaves.ponder.airship_console.text_2: Flying higher increases range. Transmitters and Relays get 50 percent more range for every 100 blocks above the ground
airwaves.ponder.airship_console.text_3: The Radio Console controls every radio block within 8 blocks of it. On a ship, that means the ship's own radio room
airwaves.ponder.airship_console.text_4: Right-click it to seek the next station. Sneak-click it to see a report of everything it controls
airwaves.ponder.airship_console.text_5: Here it controls the ship's Receiver, which plays through a PA Horn at the back
airwaves.ponder.airship_console.text_6: A Redstone signal puts all of its Transmitters on standby. A Comparator can read the signal strength
airwaves.ponder.airship_console.text_7: Cables can connect a ship to the ground, but they snap if pulled more than a quarter past their maximum length
airwaves.ponder.airship_console.text_8: Radio blocks have airship weights. Big Transmitters are heavy, small blocks are light
airwaves.ponder.studio_extras.text_1: On Air Signs are placed on walls, facing the way you click
airwaves.ponder.studio_extras.text_2: When a Transmitter within 12 blocks is sending a voice...
airwaves.ponder.studio_extras.text_3: ...the sign lights up red, so everyone knows you are live
airwaves.ponder.studio_extras.text_4: PA Horns can be mounted on posts and walls to play a Receiver's sound outside
airwaves.ponder.creative_blocks.text_1: These creative blocks are useful for testing radio setups
airwaves.ponder.creative_blocks.text_2: The Creative Transmitter needs no Antenna, Amethyst or Rotational Force. It can be heard everywhere
airwaves.ponder.creative_blocks.text_3: The Creative Antenna counts as a full Antenna of any size. Place it on the Copper behind a Transmitter or Receiver
airwaves.ponder.creative_blocks.text_4: Hold right-click on the value box on its base to set its range, from 0 to 9999 blocks
airwaves.ponder.creative_blocks.text_5: The Transmitter in front of it then reaches exactly that far
airwaves.ponder.creative_blocks.text_6: The Creative Receiver hears its station from anywhere, and Jammers do not affect it
airwaves.ponder.tape_player.text_1: The Tape Player records sounds onto Tapes and plays them back
airwaves.ponder.tape_player.text_2: Right-click it with a Tape to load it, then right-click it empty-handed to open its screen
airwaves.ponder.tape_player.text_3: Press Record. It has its own microphone: anything said within 6 blocks goes on the Tape, and so does every sound within 8, like note blocks, jukebox discs and mobs. A Tape holds up to 5 minutes
airwaves.ponder.tape_player.text_4: Press Record again to stop. Play plays it back, and Loop repeats it forever. Rename a Tape in an Anvil to label it
airwaves.ponder.tape_player.text_5: Wire it to a Transmitter like a Microphone, and whatever the Tape plays goes on air
airwaves.ponder.tape_player.text_6: Without a Wire it just plays out loud, and any wired Microphone nearby picks it up
airwaves.ponder.tape_player.text_7: A Redstone pulse starts the Tape from the beginning. Put a timer board in a Circuit Box to play shows on a schedule
block.airwaves.tape_player.tooltip.summa: Records and plays _Tapes_. _Wire_ it to a transmitter like a microphone to broadcast the tape, or leave it unwired and a nearby microphone picks it up. Turn on _Loop_ for a station that never stops.
block.airwaves.tape_player.tooltip.behav: Opens the player. _REC_ records _voices_ within 6 blocks plus every sound and jukebox disc within 8.
Starts the tape from the top: schedule shows with a _Circuit Box_ timer.
item.airwaves.tape.tooltip.summary: A cassette for the _Tape Player_. Holds up to _5 minutes_. Rename it in an anvil to label it.
item.airwaves.copper_wire.tooltip.summar: A data cable for _audio_. Reaches _16 blocks_ and loses a little quality on every block.
item.airwaves.copper_wire.tooltip.behavi: Click the first jack, then the second. Sneak-click a jack to cut its cables.
item.airwaves.gold_wire.tooltip.summary: A data cable with better contacts. Reaches _24 blocks_ with _half the loss_ of copper.
item.airwaves.gold_wire.tooltip.behaviou: Click the first jack, then the second. Sneak-click a jack to cut its cables.
item.airwaves.silver_wire.tooltip.summar: A clean signal wire. Reaches _32 blocks_ with _very little loss_.
item.airwaves.silver_wire.tooltip.behavi: Click the first jack, then the second. Sneak-click a jack to cut its cables.
item.airwaves.fiber_cable.tooltip.summar: Optical cable. Reaches _64 blocks_ with _no loss at all_.
item.airwaves.fiber_cable.tooltip.behavi: Click the first jack, then the second. Sneak-click a jack to cut its cables.
item.airwaves.multimeter.tooltip.summary: Reads out any Airwaves block: _frequency_, signal, _shaft speed_ and every cable on it.
item.airwaves.multimeter.tooltip.behavio: Shows the readout above your hotbar.
item.airwaves.frequency_card.tooltip.sum: Copies a _frequency_ from one radio block to another.
item.airwaves.frequency_card.tooltip.con: When sneak-used on a radio block
item.airwaves.frequency_card.tooltip.beh: Copies its frequency onto the card.
item.airwaves.frequency_card.tooltip.con: When used on a radio block
item.airwaves.frequency_card.tooltip.beh: Gives it the frequency on the card.
item.airwaves.circuit_board.tooltip.summ: The blank every board starts as. Finished on the _Circuit Workbench_.
block.airwaves.circuit_workbench.tooltip: Lay parts on the 6 x 4 grid and _draw copper traces_ on the empty pads so one circuit runs from _IN_ to _OUT_. The parts decide which board you get.
When a board is clicked in the list
Its layout appears as a ghost. _Auto-place_ fills it from your inventory.
item.airwaves.resistor.tooltip.summary: A circuit board part. Goes on the _Circuit Workbench_ grid.
item.airwaves.capacitor.tooltip.summary: A circuit board part. Goes on the _Circuit Workbench_ grid.
item.airwaves.led.tooltip.summary: A circuit board part. Lights up on the workbench once the board _works_.
item.airwaves.transistor.tooltip.summary: A circuit board part. Goes on the _Circuit Workbench_ grid.
item.airwaves.vacuum_tube.tooltip.summar: Amplifies. Used on _amplifier_ and _RF_ boards and inside transmitters.
item.airwaves.copper_coil.tooltip.summar: Tunes and transforms. Used on _tuner_, _RF_ and _radio_ boards, speaker cones and capsules.
item.airwaves.crystal_oscillator.tooltip: Keeps a station _on frequency_. Used on _tuner_, _RF_ and _radio_ boards.
Amethyst ground flat with _sandpaper_. Cut into crystal oscillators.
block.airwaves.antenna.tooltip.summary: Stack it on a _copper block_ behind a _small_ transmitter or receiver. Taller masts reach farther.
block.airwaves.antenna.tooltip.behaviour: Place it on top of the mast; the top piece grows a cap.
block.airwaves.antenna_medium.tooltip.su: A 2 x 2 mast for _medium_ transmitters and receivers. Must match the device size.
block.airwaves.antenna_medium.tooltip.be: Place it on top of the mast; the top piece grows a cap.
block.airwaves.antenna_big.tooltip.summa: A 3 x 3 mast for _large_ transmitters and receivers. Must match the device size.
block.airwaves.antenna_big.tooltip.behav: Place it on top of the mast; the top piece grows a cap.
block.airwaves.antenna_giant.tooltip.sum: A 4 x 4 mast for _giant_ transmitters and receivers. Must match the device size.
block.airwaves.antenna_giant.tooltip.beh: Place it on top of the mast; the top piece grows a cap.
block.airwaves.yagi_antenna.tooltip.summ: Clamps on top of an _antenna mast_ and makes it _directional_: _1.9 times_ the range ahead, a blind spot behind. Works for transmitters and receivers.
block.airwaves.yagi_antenna.tooltip.beha: Points the way you are facing. The red cap is the front.
block.airwaves.insulator.tooltip.summary: Holds cables up between devices. Up to _4 cables_ each, so lines can fork.
block.airwaves.speaker.tooltip.summary: Plays a cabled _receiver_ out loud. Several speakers can hang off one receiver.
block.airwaves.circuit_box.tooltip.summa: Runs any _circuit board_ on its own. Like a repeater: redstone in at the back, its signal out of the front. What it does is the _board's program_.
block.airwaves.circuit_box.tooltip.behav: Boards with a tuned tank listen to that station.
block.airwaves.dimensional_relay.tooltip: Carries radio _between dimensions_. Every station it hears is sent out again by every Dimensional Relay in the _Nether_ and the _End_, and the other way round. Build one on each side.
Runs on a turning _shaft_ (16 SU per RPM) or _electricity_. Keeps its own chunk loaded.
block.airwaves.relay_tower_small.tooltip: Receives a station and sends it on _farther_. Needs _power_: a shaft on the drive shaft sticking out of its base, or electricity.
Relays the station on its frequency.
block.airwaves.relay_tower_big.tooltip.s: A taller relay that _reaches farther_. Needs _power_: a shaft on the drive shaft sticking out of its base, or electricity.
block.airwaves.relay_tower_big.tooltip.b: Relays the station on its frequency.
block.airwaves.radio_tower.tooltip.summa: A whole broadcast station in one: the biggest reach there is. Needs heavy _power_: a shaft on the drive shaft sticking out of its base, or electricity.
block.airwaves.radio_tower.tooltip.behav: Connect any shaft, cog or motor to either end of the drive shaft at the edge of the base.
block.airwaves.radio_console.tooltip.sum: The control desk of a station, made for _airship bridges_. Every transmitter, receiver, relay and radio within _8 blocks_ follows its frequency.
block.airwaves.radio_console.tooltip.beh: Seeks the next station and retunes everything.
item.airwaves.portable_radio.tooltip.sum: A radio for your pocket. While it is on and in your _hotbar_ or off-hand you hear the station in your own ears.
item.airwaves.portable_radio.tooltip.beh: Seeks the next station you can hear, and switches it on.
Works as a _walkie-talkie_: every radio on the same frequency within _320 blocks_ (FM) hears you. No station needed.
block.airwaves.tuning_table.tooltip.summ: Tunes the radios, transmitters, receivers and relays you put in it. Rename one in an _anvil_ to give its station a name.
block.airwaves.creative_transmitter.tool: _Creative only._ Needs no amethyst, antenna, copper or rotation: always on the air and heard at _full quality everywhere_ in the dimension.
Microphones cable to it like any transmitter.
block.airwaves.creative_receiver.tooltip: _Creative only._ Needs no amethyst or antenna: hears the nearest station on its frequency _anywhere_, at full quality, jammers or not.
_Creative only._ One block that counts as a _complete_ antenna of whatever size the device needs. Its transmitting _range (0 to 9999 blocks)_ is set on the value box on its base.
On the copper block behind a transmitter or receiver, or right on top of a receiver.
When the value box on its base is held
A slider opens: the top row sets hundreds, the bottom row units.
block.airwaves.on_air_sign.tooltip.summa: A studio light for walls. Lights up _red_ while any transmitter within _12 blocks_ is sending a voice.
block.airwaves.horn_speaker.tooltip.summ: An outdoor loudspeaker for walls and poles. Works exactly like a _Speaker_: cable it to a receiver.
item.airwaves.tuner_board.tooltip.summar: Made on the _Circuit Workbench_. Used for: _receivers_, tuning table.
item.airwaves.amplifier_board.tooltip.su: Made on the _Circuit Workbench_. Used for: _speakers_, the giant transmitter.
item.airwaves.rf_board.tooltip.summary: Made on the _Circuit Workbench_. Used for: _transmitters_, jammer, relay towers.
item.airwaves.audio_board.tooltip.summar: Made on the _Circuit Workbench_. Used for: _microphones_.
item.airwaves.display_board.tooltip.summ: Made on the _Circuit Workbench_. Used for: _tuning table_, multimeter, giant receiver.
item.airwaves.control_board.tooltip.summ: Made on the _Circuit Workbench_. Used for: _jammer_, relay towers, radio console.
item.airwaves.radio_board.tooltip.summar: Made on the _Circuit Workbench_. Used for: _radios_, the portable radio, the radio console.
block.airwaves.transmitter_small.tooltip: Needs _amethyst_ in its chamber, a _copper block_ behind it with a small antenna on it, and _power_: a turning _shaft_ on its side (faster reaches farther) or electricity into the _red +_ and _blue -_ terminals on its front (_Create: Power Grid_ or _Create: Electro Energetics_).
Fills the chamber. Sneak-click empty-handed to take it out.
block.airwaves.receiver_small.tooltip.su: A crystal set: _amethyst_ in the chamber plus a small antenna on a _copper block_ behind it, or right on top. No power needed.
block.airwaves.receiver_small.tooltip.be: Fills the chamber. Sneak-click empty-handed to take it out.
block.airwaves.transmitter_medium.toolti: Needs _amethyst_ in its chamber, a _copper block_ behind it with a medium antenna on it, and _power_: a turning _shaft_ on its side (faster reaches farther) or electricity into the _red +_ and _blue -_ terminals on its front (_Create: Power Grid_ or _Create: Electro Energetics_).
Fills the chamber. Sneak-click empty-handed to take it out.
block.airwaves.receiver_medium.tooltip.s: A crystal set: _amethyst_ in the chamber plus a medium antenna on a _copper block_ behind it, or right on top. No power needed.
block.airwaves.receiver_medium.tooltip.b: Fills the chamber. Sneak-click empty-handed to take it out.
block.airwaves.transmitter_large.tooltip: Needs _amethyst_ in its chamber, a _copper block_ behind it with a large antenna on it, and _power_: a turning _shaft_ on its side (faster reaches farther) or electricity into the _red +_ and _blue -_ terminals on its front (_Create: Power Grid_ or _Create: Electro Energetics_).
Fills the chamber. Sneak-click empty-handed to take it out.
block.airwaves.receiver_large.tooltip.su: A crystal set: _amethyst_ in the chamber plus a large antenna on a _copper block_ behind it, or right on top. No power needed.
block.airwaves.receiver_large.tooltip.be: Fills the chamber. Sneak-click empty-handed to take it out.
